claims.text: Existing automotive exhaust catalysts contain relatively high amounts of platinum-group metals.
Existing automotive exhaust catalysts are produced by conventional synthesis methods.
The proposed intervention is a closed-loop workflow combining automated solvothermal synthesis, accelerated ageing, activity screening, machine learning, and Bayesian optimization.
The workflow iteratively refines catalyst compositions and synthesis conditions.
Closed-loop high-throughput optimization selectively enhances the formation of multi-element nanostructures.
The optimized multi-element compositions form nanostructured active sites with enhanced dispersion.
The optimized multi-element compositions form nanostructured active sites with enhanced stability.
Enhanced active-site formation and stability produce improved catalytic activity at reduced platinum loading.
Enhanced active-site formation and stability produce improved durability at reduced platinum loading.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will have statistically significantly higher turnover frequency than conventionally produced catalysts.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will retain statistically significantly more activity after accelerated ageing than conventionally produced catalysts.
Closed-loop-optimized catalysts will contain less platinum-group metal than conventionally produced catalysts with standard loadings.
The predicted improvements are expected under laboratory-simulated automotive exhaust conditions that include high temperatures and cyclic thermal ageing.
Performance may vary when synthesis parameters, elemental compatibility, or operating conditions differ substantially from those used during optimization.
Prior high-throughput methods in similar catalyst systems provide promising preliminary evidence.
The magnitude and reproducibility of the predicted improvements under actual exhaust conditions remain uncertain.
